src.text:
INTRODUCTION (what the novel is, who wrote it, when):
Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (also known as  Alice in Wonderland) is an 1865 English children's novel by Lewis Carroll. It tells the story of a little girl named Alice who falls through a rabbit hole into a fantasy world of anthropomorphic creatures. It is seen as an example of the literary nonsense genre. The artist John Tenniel provided 42 wood-engraved illustrations for the original edition.
The novel received positive reviews upon release. It has become one of the best-known works of Victorian literature; its narrative, structure, characters, and imagery have had a wide influence on popular culture and literature, especially in the fantasy genre. It is credited as helping end an era of didacticism in children's literature, inaugurating an era in which writing for children aimed to "delight or entertain". The tale plays with logic, giving the story lasting popularity with adults a

PLOT (an editor-reviewed concise summary of the whole story, 787 words; the ONLY source of the events):
Sitting with her older sister on a bank, and feeling rather sleepy and bored, Alice suddenly spots a White Rabbit with a pocket watch and waistcoat hurrying by, lamenting that he is late. Surprised, Alice follows him down a rabbit hole, which sends her into a lengthy fall. Landing safely, she finds herself inside a room where she discovers a key to a tiny door, beyond which is a garden. While pondering how to fit through the door, she notices a bottle labelled "Drink me". Alice drinks some of the contents and, to her astonishment, shrinks small enough to enter the door. However, she had left the key on a table and is now unable to reach it. She finds and eats a cake labelled "Eat me", which causes her to grow to a tremendous size. Distraught, Alice bursts into tears. As she cries, the White Rabbit rushes past, dropping a fan and gloves. Alice uses the fan to cool herself down, which causes her to shrink once more and leaves her swimming in a pool of her own tears. There she meets various animals and birds, who convene on a bank and engage in a "Caucus Race" to dry themselves. Alice inadvertently frightens the animals away by mentioning her cat.

Mistaking her for his maidservant, the White Rabbit orders Alice to go to his house and retrieve his lost gloves and fan. Alice finds another bottle and drinks from it, causing her to grow to such an extent that she gets stuck in the house. Attempting to extract her, the White Rabbit and his neighbours eventually take to hurling pebbles that turn into small cakes. Alice eats one and shrinks herself, allowing her to flee into the forest. She meets a Caterpillar seated on a mushroom and smoking a hookah. Under the Caterpillar's questioning, Alice begins to admit to her current identity crisis, compounded by her inability to remember a poem. Before crawling away, the Caterpillar says that a bite of one side of the mushroom will make her larger, while a bite from the other side will make her smaller. During a period of trial and error, Alice's neck extends between the treetops, frightening a pigeon who mistakes her for a serpent. After shrinking to an appropriate height, Alice arrives at the home of a Duchess, who owns a perpetually grinning Cheshire Cat. The Duchess's baby, whom she hands to Alice, transforms into a piglet, which Alice releases into the woods. The Cheshire Cat appears to Alice and directs her toward the Hatter and March Hare before disappearing, leaving his grin behind. Alice finds the Hatter, March Hare, and a sleepy Dormouse in the middle of a tea party. The Hatter explains that it is always 6 p.m. (tea time) – the consequence of his having quarrelled with Time. Unable to answer the riddle "Why is a raven like a writing desk?", and considering the company rude, Alice walks off, declaring "It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life!"

Noticing a door in a tree, Alice passes through and finds herself back in the room from the beginning of her journey. She takes the key and opens the door to the garden, which turns out to be the croquet court of the Queen of Hearts, whose guard consists of living playing cards. Alice participates in a croquet game, in which hedgehogs are used as balls, flamingos are used as mallets, and soldiers act as hoops. The Queen is short-tempered, constantly ordering beheadings. When the Cheshire Cat's lone head appears, the Queen orders its beheading, an act which appears impossible in the absence of a body from which to sever it. Alice prompts the Queen to release the Duchess, now in prison.
Alice meets a Gryphon and a Mock Turtle, who dance to the Lobster Quadrille while Alice recites (rather incorrectly) a poem. The Mock Turtle sings "Beautiful Soup", during which the Gryphon drags Alice away for a trial, in which the Knave of Hearts stands accused of stealing the Queen's tarts. The trial is conducted by the King of Hearts, and the jury is composed of animals that Alice previously met. Alice gradually grows in size and confidence, allowing herself increasingly frequent remarks on the irrationality of the proceedings. The Queen eventually commands Alice's beheading, but Alice scoffs that her guard is only a pack of playing cards. The cards rise up into the air and come swarming down upon her.
Alice wakes from her dream to find her sister brushing leaves from her face. Alice tells her about her adventures, then runs in for her tea, leaving her sister on the bank to imagine all the curious happenings for herself.

SIGNIFICANCE (themes, reception, legacy: use ONLY for the closing wrap-up, to say why the novel matters):
[Writing style and themes]
Symbolism: Carroll's biographer Morton N. Cohen reads Alice as a roman à clef populated with real figures from Carroll's life. Alice is based on Alice Liddell; the Dodo is Carroll; Wonderland is Oxford; even the Mad Hatter's Tea Party, according to Cohen, is a send-up of Alice's own birthday party. The critic Jan Susina rejects Cohen's account, arguing that Alice the character bears a tenuous relationship with Alice Liddell.
Beyond its refashioning of Carroll's everyday life, Cohen argues, Alice critiques Victorian ideals of childhood. It is an account of "the child's plight in Victorian upper-class society", in which Alice's mistreatment by the creatures of Wonderland reflects Carroll's own mistreatment by older people as a child.
In the eighth chapter, three cards are painting the roses 

[Reception]
Alice was published to critical praise. One magazine declared it "exquisitely wild, fantastic, [and] impossible". In the late 19th century, Walter Besant wrote that Alice in Wonderland "was a book of that extremely rare kind which will belong to all the generations to come until the language becomes obsolete".

No story in English literature has intrigued me more than Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland. It fascinated me the first time I read it as a schoolboy.
F. J. Harvey Darton argued in a 1932 book that Alice ended an era of didacticism in children's literature, inaugurating a new era in which writing for children aimed to "delight or entertain".

scenes.spoken_fa: قبل از اینکه Caterpillar خزیده و دور شود، به او گفت که یک طرف قارچ او را بزرگ‌تر و طرف دیگر او را کوچک‌تر می‌کند. پس از آزمون و خطاهای بسیار، گردن Alice آن‌قدر بلند شد که میان درختان جنگل قرار گرفت و کبوتری را ترساند که او را با یک مار اشتباه گرفته بود. بعد از اینکه قدش به اندازه معمول برگشت، او به خانه یک Duchess رسید که یک Cheshire Cat همیشه خندان را داشت.

بعد از اینکه قدش به اندازه معمول برگشت، او به خانه یک Duchess رسید که یک Cheshire Cat همیشه خندان را داشت.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Caterpillar crawls slowly across the cap of a large spotted mushroom, surrounded by green ferns and damp soil on the forest floor.
Alice stretches her long neck high up among the green branches and leaves of tall forest trees, looking down at startled birds.
Alice stands outside a crooked country cottage with a thatched roof, looking at a grinning cat perched on a wooden fence post.

scenes.narration_fa: پس از آن، او به یک مهمانی چای عجیب وارد شد که در آن Mad Hatter و March Hare و یک Dormouse خواب‌آلود حضور داشتند. Mad Hatter توضیح داد که زمان همیشه روی ساعت شش عصر متوقف مانده است چون او با زمان دعوا کرده بود. از آنجا که پاسخ معما را نمی‌دانست و رفتار میزبانان را بی‌ادبانه دید، Alice آنجا را ترک کرد. سپس او از درختی گذشت و دوباره به همان اتاق آغازین برگشت تا این‌که کلید را برداشت و وارد باغ شد.
scenes.source_en: Alice finds the Hatter, March Hare, and a sleepy Dormouse in the middle of a tea party. The Hatter explains that it is always 6 p.m. (tea time) – the consequence of his having quarrelled with Time. Unable to answer the riddle Why is a raven like a writing desk?, and considering the company rude, Alice walks off, declaring It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life! Noticing a door in a tree, Alice passes through and finds herself back in the room from the beginning of her journey. She takes the key and opens the door to the garden
scenes.setting_en: A long outdoor table set for tea under the trees
scenes.action_en: Mad Hatter and friends are sitting at the table while Alice walks away in frustration
scenes.mood_en: Nonsensical and eccentric tea party setting with pastel colors

beat_visuals.visual_en: Mad Hatter sits at a long outdoor table laden with teapots and cups, surrounded by scattered chairs in a shady garden.
Mad Hatter pours hot tea from a metal teapot into a china cup on a wooden table, under the branches of an old willow tree.
Alice opens a small wooden door built into the trunk of a massive ancient tree, revealing bright sunlight shining from the other side.

scenes.narration_fa: آن باغ در واقع زمین بازی کروکت ملکه یعنی Queen of Hearts بود که سربازانش کارت‌های بازی زنده بودند. بازی کروکت با جوجه تیغی‌ها به عنوان توپ و فلامینگوها به عنوان چوب بازی انجام می‌شد و ملکه بسیار زودرنج بود و مدام دستور سر بریدن صادر می‌کرد. وقتی سر Cheshire Cat ظاهر شد، ملکه دستور داد سرش را بزنند در حالی که اصلا بدنی وجود نداشت. بعد از آن Alice به ملاقات یک موجود عجیب و Mock Turtle رفت و رقص لابس‌تر را تماشا کرد.
scenes.source_en: which turns out to be the croquet court of the Queen of Hearts, whose guard consists of living playing cards. Alice participates in a croquet game, in which hedgehogs are used as balls, flamingos are used as mallets, and soldiers act as hoops. The Queen is short-tempered, constantly ordering beheadings. When the Cheshire Cat's lone head appears, the Queen orders its beheading, an act which appears impossible in the absence of a body from which to sever it. Alice meets a Gryphon and a Mock Turtle, who dance to the Lobster Quadrille
scenes.setting_en: A bright royal garden with trimmed hedges and playing card guards
scenes.action_en: Queen of Hearts is shouting angrily during a croquet game while Alice holds a flamingo
scenes.mood_en: Tense and chaotic royal atmosphere with bright reds and greens

beat_visuals.visual_en: Queen of Hearts stands on a manicured lawn holding a wooden mallet, glaring angrily at living playing cards acting as soldiers.
Alice watches a fantastical turtle-like creature dancing on a sandy beach near the ocean, under a bright sunny sky.

scenes.narration_fa: سپس او به یک دادگاه کشیده شد که در آن Knave of Hearts متهم شده بود تارت‌های ملکه را دزدیده است. ریاست دادگاه بر عهده King of Hearts بود و هیئت منصفه را همان حیواناتی تشکیل می‌دادند که Alice قبلاً دیده بود. در جریان دادگاه، Alice به تدریج بزرگ‌تر شد و اعتمادبه‌نفس بیشتری پیدا کرد تا جایی که به بی‌منطقی این محاکمه اعتراض کرد. وقتی ملکه خشمگین دستور داد سر او را قطع کنند، Alice گفت آن‌ها فقط یک دست ورق بازی هستند.
scenes.source_en: the Gryphon drags Alice away for a trial, in which the Knave of Hearts stands accused of stealing the Queen's tarts. The trial is conducted by the King of Hearts, and the jury is composed of animals that Alice previously met. Alice gradually grows in size and confidence, allowing herself increasingly frequent remarks on the irrationality of the proceedings. The Queen eventually commands Alice's beheading, but Alice scoffs that her guard is only a pack of playing cards.
scenes.setting_en: A large indoor courtroom with a raised throne and animal jury
scenes.action_en: Alice stands tall in the courtroom looking down bravely at the angry Queen on her throne
scenes.mood_en: Dramatic and climactic courtroom scene with stark red and black decor

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice stands in a crowded courtroom with wooden benches, surrounded by animal jurors holding pencils and notepads during a trial.
Queen of Hearts points an accusing finger forward in a grand hall, while Alice stands bravely facing her with an expression of defiance.

scenes.narration_fa: در جمع‌بندی، این سفر عجیب با فرود آمدن Alice از لانه خرگوش آغاز شد و با شورش او علیه کارت‌های بازی در دادگاه به نقطه اوج رسید. این رمان با چالش کشیدن منطق و پایان دادن به عصر ادبیات آموزشی کودکان، دوره جدیدی از سرگرمی را بنیان گذاشت که تا به امروز در فرهنگ عامه ماندگار است. با هجوم کارت‌های بازی به سمت او، Alice ناگهان از خواب بیدار شد و دید که خواهرش برگ‌ها را از روی صورتش پاک می‌کند. او ماجراهای خود را تعریف کرد و برای خوردن چای به خانه دوید و خوابش را تمام کرد.
scenes.source_en: The cards rise up into the air and come swarming down upon her. Alice wakes from her dream to find her sister brushing leaves from her face. Alice tells her about her adventures, then runs in for her tea, leaving her sister on the bank to imagine all the curious happenings for herself.
scenes.setting_en: The same peaceful grassy riverbank from the very beginning of the story
scenes.action_en: Alice wakes up rubbing her eyes while her sister gently brushes dry leaves from her hair
scenes.mood_en: Peaceful, dreamy, and heartwarming conclusion with warm golden sunlight

beat_visuals.visual_en: Playing cards swirl upward into the dark air like a tornado of paper, hovering above Alice who stands bewildered on a stone floor.
An old open storybook lies on a grassy green lawn, its pages fluttering in a gentle breeze under the warm afternoon sun.
Alice wakes up lying on the grass under a large tree, opening her eyes while her sister gently brushes green leaves from her hair.
Alice runs excitedly across a sunny green lawn toward a country house, waving her hands and smiling brightly on a peaceful afternoon.
